title: Enrollment Reinstatement Review: Good Cause and Past-Due Payment
content:
## Enrollment Reinstatement Review — Appeals and Grievances

**Clause.** An Enrollment Reinstatement Review asks to reverse a disenrollment or termination for nonpayment. It is decided overturned only when a statement of good cause documenting one of the tier's good cause examples is on file and the circumstance covers the due date that was missed; forgetting, a changed bank account the beneficiary did not report, or disagreement with the fee amount are not good cause. The enrollment is reinstated only after every past-due fee or premium through the current period is paid. A reinstatement request about an enrollment that was not ended for nonpayment is dismissed as not appealable. A reinstatement is decided overturned only when a statement of good cause is on file for the case — read from the documents received for that case.

**Circumstance tested against the missed due date**

| Statement of good cause on file for the case | Circumstance is a listed good cause example | It covers the missed due date | Decided overturned possible |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | — | — | no |
| yes | no (for example forgetting, an unreported change of bank account, disagreement with the fee amount) | — | no |
| yes | yes | no | no |
| yes | yes | yes | yes |

**Hypothetical cases**

- A sponsor's deployment began before the missed due date and is documented in a statement of good cause on file: the circumstance is a listed example and covers the due date, so the review may be decided overturned; reinstatement then follows only once every past-due fee or premium through the current period is paid.
- A beneficiary forgot the payment: not good cause.
- The enrollment ended because the beneficiary left the region, not for nonpayment: the request is dismissed as not appealable.
